outcome: Prevalence of extended spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) producing Escherichia coli
cohort: 200 children visiting Primary Health Centers in Surabaya, Indonesia
finding: The prevalence of ESBL-producing E. coli was significantly higher in post-neonatal children compared to neonates, and risk factors included history of hospital visits, maternal antibiotic use, and mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was a significant risk factor for ESBL-producing E. coli in both neonatal and post-neonatal children.
